t: Merik — Workforce Suite
d: Merik is an all-in-one workforce management platform for small and growing businesses — employee management, attendance tracking, leave, payroll, daily task tracking, clients, invoicing and assets in one secure company workspace.

t: Features
d: Explore Merik's features: employee management, attendance tracking, leave management, payroll, daily task tracking and secure company workspaces — everything HR needs in one platform.

t: How it works
d: See how Merik works in three steps: create your company workspace, invite your people, then run daily attendance, leave, tasks and payroll — set up in under five minutes.

t: Modules
d: Merik's modules cover the whole workforce: employees, attendance, leave & WFH, payroll, daily tasks, performance, and clients, projects, quotes & invoices — all in one workspace.

t: Pricing
d: Merik pricing: create a company workspace free, with unlimited employee self sign-up, attendance, leave, payroll, payslips, daily tasks, clients and invoicing. No setup fee, no card required.

t: ROI calculator
d: Work out what attendance, leave and payroll admin costs your business each year. Move four sliders for a live estimate in rupees and hours — with the assumptions shown, not hidden.

t: Payroll & HR glossary
d: Plain-English definitions of 20 Indian payroll and workforce terms — CTC, gross and net salary, LOP, HRA, provident fund, earned leave, encashment, notice period and full and final settlement, each with a worked example.

t: How to track employee attendance in a small business (without spreadsheets)
d: A practical step-by-step guide to tracking employee attendance accurately in a small business — the problems with spreadsheets, what to record, and how to feed attendance straight into payroll.

t: Biometric vs GPS vs manual attendance: which should you use?
d: A practical comparison of biometric, GPS and manual attendance tracking for small businesses — cost, accuracy, and which fits office, field and hybrid teams.

t: How to calculate late marks and half-days fairly
d: A clear, consistent rule set for late marks and half-days — grace periods, thresholds, and how to connect them to payroll deductions without disputes.

t: Geolocation attendance for field and multi-site teams
d: How GPS-based check-in works for field, site and multi-location teams — what to capture, how to keep it fair and privacy-safe, and how location-verified attendance feeds payroll.

t: Attendance policy template for a small business (copy and adapt)
d: A complete attendance policy template for small businesses — working hours, grace periods, late marks, half-days, leave interaction, remote work and corrections, in plain language you can adapt today.

t: Attendance regularisation: fixing a wrong day without breaking trust
d: How to handle missed punches and attendance corrections properly — the request-and-approve flow, deadlines, audit trails, and why editing the register in place quietly destroys your payroll evidence.

t: From attendance to payroll: how to stop re-keying numbers every month
d: Learn how connecting attendance and leave directly to payroll removes errors, saves hours at month-end, and produces accurate monthly pay — a practical guide for small businesses.

t: CTC vs in-hand salary: how to read a payslip (India guide)
d: Understand CTC vs in-hand salary and how to read a payslip in India — gross pay, allowances, deductions like PF and professional tax, and how net pay is calculated each month.

t: Payroll compliance checklist for Indian small businesses
d: A practical payroll compliance checklist for small businesses in India — PF, ESI, professional tax and TDS basics, and what to get right every month.

t: How to run payroll for a small team without an accountant
d: A practical monthly payroll process for founders and office managers running payroll for a 10-50 person team without a dedicated accountant.

t: Common payroll mistakes small businesses make
d: The recurring payroll mistakes small businesses make — from re-keying errors to missed salary hikes — and how to avoid them each month.

t: Payslip format: what every payslip must show (and why)
d: A complete guide to payslip format — the earnings, deductions and attendance lines every payslip should carry, why each one matters, and how to produce payslips employees can verify themselves.

t: Loss of pay (LOP): how it's calculated, with worked examples
d: How loss of pay is calculated in monthly payroll — the calendar-days vs working-days divisor debate settled with actual arithmetic, plus half-days, mid-month joins and the mistakes that cause wrong salaries.

t: Running a salary hike cycle without guesswork
d: How to run a salary revision cycle in a small business — budgeting the pot, deciding increments, effective dates, arrears, communicating revisions, and keeping a clean CTC history for every employee.

t: Paid vs unpaid leave: how to manage employee leave in a small business
d: A practical guide to managing employee leave in a small business — paid vs unpaid leave, how to track balances, approve requests, and keep monthly payroll accurate.

t: How many leaves should a small business offer in India?
d: A practical benchmark for annual, sick and casual leave policies for small businesses in India, and how to structure a leave policy employees understand.

t: Work from home policy: what to include and how to track it
d: A simple work-from-home policy template for small businesses — what to cover, how many WFH days to allow, and how to track it alongside attendance.

t: Sick leave vs casual leave: what's the difference?
d: Sick leave vs casual leave explained — how they differ, why the distinction matters, and how to keep your leave policy consistent for both.

t: Leave carry-forward and encashment, explained simply
d: How leave carry-forward and encashment work — caps, lapse rules, encashment formulas, the year-end liability nobody budgets for, and how to design a policy that doesn't create a surprise bill.

t: How to build a company holiday calendar (India)
d: How to plan a company holiday calendar — national and state holidays, fixed vs restricted holidays, how many to offer, publishing it in advance, and why payroll depends on the calendar being right.

t: Daily task tracking for small teams: proof, blockers & accountability
d: How to run daily task tracking for a small team — assign work, capture proof and blockers, and build accountability without micromanaging or drowning in status meetings.

t: How to run daily standups without a meeting
d: Get the same visibility as a daily standup meeting without the calendar invite — a written async update flow that respects everyone's time.

t: Measuring productivity without micromanaging
d: How to measure team productivity by tracking outcomes and proof instead of screen time or constant check-ins — and keep your team's trust.

t: Timesheets vs daily task logs: which one does your team need?
d: The practical difference between a timesheet and a daily task log — what each captures, which one your team will actually fill in, and how to get billing accuracy without weekly reconstruction.

t: Why your time estimates are always wrong (and how to fix them)
d: Why software and services estimates run over, how to measure estimate accuracy from your own task log, and a practical method for improving estimation using historical data instead of optimism.

t: How to structure clients and projects so reporting actually works
d: Get the client-project hierarchy right once and every report downstream is free. How to name projects, avoid free-typed entries, handle retainers vs one-off work, and fix a messy history.

t: The quote-to-invoice workflow for a small services business
d: How to run quoting and invoicing as one connected flow — line-item quotes, approval, converting a quote to an invoice without retyping, what every invoice must show, and chasing payment without awkwardness.

t: Working out project profitability from your task hours
d: How to calculate real project profitability using the hours your team already logs — building a loaded hourly cost, allocating overhead, worked examples, and what to do when a favourite client turns out to be unprofitable.

t: How to price a retainer using your own time data
d: Stop guessing the monthly retainer number. How to size a retainer from logged hours, price the three retainer models, handle overage and scope creep, and set the renewal price from delivered data.

t: IT asset management for small businesses: the register you actually need
d: How to build a hardware asset register that stays accurate — what fields to track, assignment and return workflows, tying assets to employee exit, and the audit routine that keeps it honest.

t: Software subscription spend: finding the seats nobody uses
d: A practical monthly routine for controlling SaaS spend in a small business — building the subscription register, tying seats to employees, finding waste at offboarding, and renegotiating at renewal.

t: Employee onboarding checklist for small businesses
d: A practical employee onboarding checklist for small businesses — what to set up before day one, during week one, and in the first month.

t: Structuring departments and designations as you scale
d: How to organize departments and designations before your team outgrows an informal structure — a practical guide for growing small businesses.

t: Employee self-service: what it means and why it matters
d: What employee self-service actually means for a small business, and how it removes HR as a bottleneck for attendance, leave and daily updates.

t: Employee exit and full & final settlement
d: How to handle employee exits and full and final settlement in a small business — what to check, what to calculate, and how to close out cleanly.

t: Choosing HR software for a small business: a buyer's checklist
d: What to look for before choosing HR software for a small business — a practical buyer's checklist covering attendance, leave, payroll, tasks and self-service.

t: A monthly performance review process that takes 20 minutes
d: How to run short monthly performance reviews grounded in work already logged — the four-question format, avoiding recency bias, what to write down, and how monthly notes make the annual review trivial.

t: Workforce data security: what to check before you upload your team
d: The questions to ask any HR or payroll tool before it holds your salaries, IDs and bank details — tenant isolation, access control, encryption, where salary maths runs, backups, exports and vendor exit.

t: AI in HR software: what actually helps, and what's theatre
d: A clear-eyed look at AI in HR and workforce tools — where language models genuinely save time, where simple statistics beat them, and the decisions AI must never make about employees.

t: Migrating from spreadsheets to workforce software: a 30-day plan
d: A week-by-week plan for moving attendance, leave, payroll and task tracking off spreadsheets — what to migrate, what to leave behind, how to run one month in parallel, and how to avoid breaking payroll.

t: What Is Proactive Application Monitoring? (Plain-English Guide)
d: Proactive application monitoring detects errors, failures and abnormal behaviour before users report them. What it is, how it differs from reactive monitoring, what to watch, and how to start.

t: Application Health Monitoring: The Complete Guide (2026)
d: A complete guide to application health monitoring — availability, latency, error rates, frontend health, API health, health scores, alerting and early warnings, with a practical rollout plan.

t: What Should You Monitor in a SaaS Application? The Complete Checklist
d: A practical SaaS monitoring checklist — uptime, APIs, frontend errors, certificates, performance baselines, dependencies and deployments — with priorities and the reasoning behind each item.

t: Application Monitoring for Startups: What to Monitor First
d: A pragmatic monitoring guide for startups — what to monitor first with two engineers and no budget, what to defer, and how to get early warnings without building an observability stack.

t: Frontend Errors: Why Users See Problems Before Your Team Does
d: Frontend errors break pages your server delivered perfectly — JavaScript exceptions, failed requests, broken UI. Why server-side monitoring misses them and how frontend error monitoring works.

t: How to Monitor JavaScript Console Errors in Production
d: Console errors in production are real failures happening to real users. How to capture uncaught exceptions and rejections at scale, group them, protect privacy, and alert on what matters.

t: Backend Errors That Break Your Product Without Crashing It
d: The dangerous backend failures are the quiet ones — 500s on one route, timeouts, degraded dependencies, wrong responses. How to detect partial backend failure from the outside.

t: The Hidden Cost of Silent Application Failures
d: Silent failures — errors nobody sees, jobs that stop, data that quietly never saves — cost revenue, trust and data integrity long before anyone notices. What they cost and how to surface them.

t: How to Detect API Failures Before Your Customers Do
d: API failures rarely start as outages — they start as timeouts, 5xx trickles and latency climbs. How to monitor APIs per endpoint and catch failures before customers report them.

t: 10 Production Issues Your Monitoring Should Detect Automatically
d: From API failures and JavaScript errors to expiring certificates and dead background jobs — the ten production issues a monitoring setup should catch without a human watching.

t: Your Application Is Up. So Why Are Users Still Having Problems?
d: Uptime says 100%, users say broken — both are telling the truth. The gap between server health and user experience, where it comes from, and how to monitor what users actually get.

t: The Complete Guide to Proactive Application Reliability
d: The cornerstone guide: how monitoring, baselines, early warnings, error budgets, incident response and deploy correlation combine into a reliability practice that prevents incidents instead of narrating them.

t: What Is Observability? How It Differs From Monitoring
d: Monitoring tells you something is wrong; observability helps you understand why. Clear definitions, the three pillars, where each approach fits, and where proactive detection sits in the evolution.

t: Why Logs Alone Are Not Enough for Modern Application Monitoring
d: Logs are records, not lookouts: nobody reads them until after the incident. Why log-based operations detect problems late, what logs are actually for, and the monitoring layer that belongs in front of them.

t: How AI Helps Detect Application Problems Before They Become Incidents
d: Where machine intelligence genuinely helps monitoring — baselines, anomaly detection, correlation, noise reduction — and where the marketing outruns the capability. An honest map.

t: Reactive vs Proactive Monitoring: What's the Difference?
d: Reactive monitoring responds to failures; proactive monitoring detects the deterioration that precedes them. A clear side-by-side, the cost asymmetry, and how teams move from one to the other.

t: Why Waiting for Users to Report Bugs Is Too Late
d: User reports are the slowest, lossiest bug detector available — most users never report, and the reports that arrive lack everything diagnostic. How teams detect production issues first.

t: How to Detect Broken User Flows Before Customers Complain
d: Signup, login, checkout — flows break at their weakest step while every component looks healthy. How to monitor multi-step user journeys and catch flow breakage early.

t: How to Reduce MTTD (Mean Time to Detect) for Application Issues
d: MTTD is the silent half of incident duration — the gap between a problem starting and anyone knowing. What drives detection lag and the six changes that cut it from hours to minutes.

t: How Proactive Monitoring Stops Small Bugs Becoming Major Incidents
d: Incidents are rarely born big — they escalate: small error, repeated error, degradation, outage, customer impact. How early detection interrupts the chain at its cheapest link.
